project.summary: DAI Harness is a local-first, provider-neutral engineering orchestration toolkit with an evidence-backed six-phase delivery pipeline and optional domain capability packs.

roots.purpose: Canonical boot, solve, verification, clarification, audit, and escalation contracts.
Senior specialist skills and shared pipeline protocols used by routed roles.
Canonical TypeScript MCP runtime, middleware, tools, and runtime tests.
Project initialization, onboarding, Docs Hub, and local operator commands.
Provider-neutral local CI, release, setup, synchronization, and runtime automation.
Machine-readable public and internal data contracts.
Product, architecture, roadmap, workflow, operations, and migration sources rendered by Docs Hub.
Repository-level deterministic unit, integration, contract, hook, and release verification.
Project-owned templates installed or synchronized into supported client workspaces.

backlog.title: Identify the active agent runtime and optimize subagent routing with current token prices
acceptance: Every request identifies the active execution surface, provider, capability source, and available concurrency before dispatch planning.
Every candidate subagent model is compared using current first-party input, cached-input, and output token pricing; missing or host-specific actual cost stays explicitly UNVERIFIED.
Routing prioritizes acceptance effectiveness, then wall-clock speed, total tokens, and estimated token cost; small coupled work records no-spawn.
A cheaper model is rejected when its retry, verification, or critical-path risk makes the overall plan less effective.

backlog.title: Wire the change-aware Docs Hub gate into precommit, full local CI, and required release checks

Strict doctor and a fresh temporary HTML/CSS build pass without modifying source files.
Precommit and provider-neutral required checks invoke the same local gate.

The portal is usable at mobile and desktop widths without horizontal viewport overflow.

backlog.title: Close legacy evidence, traceability, payment routing, RED-GREEN, signed-review, and dirty-tree bypasses
acceptance: Schema v1 and trivial or unrelated verifier evidence cannot complete code changes.
Every acceptance ID maps to exact concrete invoked test references and the machine-derived execution manifest matches the command.
Every negative_paths entry has an exact negative_path_bindings record with an ID, acceptance IDs, and invoked refs.
Every final-tree verifier is replayed from its exact stored argv; a nonzero, missing, timed-out, or worktree-mutating command blocks completion.
Payment, billing, IAP, receipt, entitlement, subscription, and checkout work is always HARD/DEEP and requires contract, runtime, E2E, and signed review-2 evidence.
Fixes require the same verifier RED to GREEN chain; HARD fixes also require pre-mutation GREEN, mutation failure, and exact final GREEN with tree restoration.

Only OpenSSH Ed25519 review-2 signatures trusted by external DAIHARNESS_REVIEW_ALLOWED_SIGNERS or ~/.daiharness/reviewers.allowed_signers can approve HARD work; review-1/self-authored JSON is UNVERIFIED.
Any staged, unstaged, tracked, or untracked nonignored source change invalidates prior evidence; secrets and private keys stay outside the workspace.

Verifier-owned evidence and volatile runtime memory, session, telemetry, cache, and review-handoff state cannot invalidate evidence merely by operating; arbitrary ignored project content remains fingerprinted.
An opaque platform-native Codex turn_id cannot shadow current evidence; selection is frozen once, while mapped-but-invalid selectors and non-correlated responses block.
Evidence and linked review reads are bounded regular-file operations that reject symlinks, path escape, and schema-v2 turn-to-filename mismatches.

status.summary: An audit of the host-resource runtime on Windows found the runtime did not work there at all, and the cause was one missing environment variable. host_resources.command() hands its child only PATH, LC_ALL and LANG, and PowerShell cannot start without SystemRoot: the memory probe exited 0xFFFF0000 in 0.18s with 'Loading managed Windows PowerShell failed', the except clause swallowed it, and memory_snapshot() returned MemorySnapshot(0, 0, 'unknown', 'telemetry-unavailable'). Those zeros are not inert: select_jobs tests available_bytes - reserved - memory_bytes < headroom, which with available at 0 and headroom at 1 GiB holds for every row, so every job was denied insufficient-memory on a host with 31.8 GiB installed and 12.7 GiB free -- reproduced end to end. No test caught it because every test in the suite injects a synthetic sensor, one of them saying so outright. The probe now reads GlobalMemoryStatusEx in process: no child, so no environment, PATH, execution policy or startup cost to get wrong, and 8 ms instead of the 1.0-1.3s a PowerShell start measured here against a 2s timeout. Separately, an argv list stops being an argv list when the target is a batch file: Windows has no argv, list2cmdline quotes only on a space or tab, so x&echo.SPLIT arrives bare and cmd.exe splits it and runs the tail -- measured through both a %* and a %1 shim. validate() now refuses a .cmd or .bat target, because the runtime cannot control what the target does with its command line and the journal's argv_sha256 would otherwise describe an argv that is not what ran. Four other suspicions were measured and are not defects: st_dev gives distinct stable volume identities, O_EXCL still refuses an existing redirect where O_NOFOLLOW is absent, the POSIX ps PATH in resource_controls is unreachable on Windows, and host_inventory's /bin/ps raises but snapshot() catches it and reports sensor-unavailable rather than inventing rows. The finding that was left for a decision has been decided. A file created 0o600 lands 0o666 on Windows and private_mode_is_safe reports success there by design, so the journal guard could not refuse any input on that platform; ADR-014 adopts containment in the user profile as the Windows private-state basis, and private_root_is_verifiable now establishes it at the four points that create a private state root rather than the twenty that read one. Surveying for the same gap found a different defect: runtime_registry wrote the RLG lease log -- the audit trail of every project path, session id, pid and command line the guard ever opened -- with no ownership, mode or redirect check on any platform, an absent check rather than a vacuous one, and it is now established with the same basis and opened O_NOFOLLOW, with a home this user owns but left too open tightened rather than refused so existing installations keep working. A third suspicion was measured and retracted: workspace-rooted job storage is not exposed, because CPython translates a directory's mode=0o700 into a restrictive DACL and secure_paths.mkdir_at passes that mode by default, so the runtime's own creation path is already private by the same mechanism POSIX uses. No ACL is written, since that would duplicate what the platform already did; a reader and a tripwire test pin the behaviour instead, because it is a platform detail rather than a documented guarantee -- and because a file's own mode buys nothing on Windows, where privacy comes from the directory holding the file.
